scope.runtime: Private AOT baseline and private compact-header variant from the frozen managed-gzip production libraries. No posting cache or tighter eligibility changes. Same SQLite copy, separate sequential capped services; live 2M producer untouched.
scope.sampling: One prepared/warm pair per query/filter. Shared CPU/I/O load, so individual differences are exploratory and not controlled speedup estimates.
scope.memory: Both services use MemoryMax=2000000000/MemorySwapMax=0; baseline cgroup peak76746752B and variant75653120B. This measures queries on 100k, not production 2M capacity.
scope.coverage: search, metadata, create, archive import; each unfiltered, group:email and imap. All 24 ordered 100-ID lists identical to frozen baseline. Only 34 lexical expansion terms indexed for this proof; fallback uses original postings for absent companion terms. No general migration implemented.
scope.format: Scratch candidateheaders table only. Production schema 6/posting 5 unchanged. Each companion row is AES-GCM-authenticated gzip of 16 existing 168-byte headers; exact bitmap/TF/boost bytes copied from authenticated existing postings. Full positions/scoring remain in original rows.
scope.limit: The existing exact posting-header bounds are preserved. Packing reduces candidate authentication calls but does not tighten bounds or prove 500ms at 2M.
scope.cacheInteraction: Savings are not additive with candidate-payload reuse: compact headers omit positions, so scoring still decrypts original postings. When nearly every group scores, cache-only can outperform header-only. Companion headers need tighter pruning or measured cache pressure to justify integration.

noFormatLazyPruningAssessment: Current per-term128-document maxTF/boost and term-presence bounds live only inside encrypted posting rows. Term dictionary exposes DF, not score-impact bounds. Unopened rows may contain higher field boosts or phrase matches, so a universal18-point field-boost/+4phrase envelope cannot safely stop ordinary top100 retrieval early. Lazy iteration alone may fuse passes but cannot generally avoid unopened rows.
migrationProposalNotImplemented: Build companion chunks from existing authenticated postings, never reread conversation bodies. Publish complete term routes atomically with a persisted migration checkpoint; unindexed/incomplete terms must retain the existing path.
Update dirty companion chunks in the same transaction as original posting mutations. Chunk size16 bounds recompression input to2688B per affected term/chunk before optional phrase intervals.
Avoid duplicating single-posting rare terms if measurements justify it; original exact fallback remains valid. Route completeness and crossing the indexing threshold require explicit atomic handling.

Companion headers can append per-term/per128-block min/max position intervals (8B each) for conservative phrase-bound intersection, yielding232B per posting page/3712B per16-page chunk. Preserve unsupported numeric/single-character phrase fallback.

Measure update/write amplification and complete-index size before adopting. In these34 terms, average sealed companion row is about1197B vs471B per original row; a small change can therefore add roughly2.5times the existing per-row write bytes. This is a measured sample ratio, not total-workload amplification.
diagnosis: Candidate-phase packaging is validated independently, but the main remaining numeric work is unchanged. No universal no-format lazy-pruning solution follows from these results.
